headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risks from AutoGPT feeding plano via files/APIs; no direct evidence of shared isolation or verification.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGPT can read and write filesystem content and call agent protocol APIs, while plano consumes OpenAI-compatible chat inputs and config files. That creates a plausible path for AutoGPT-generated content to be treated as instructions by plano. No direct shared-channel evidence is provided, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF AutoGPT writes prompt-like text into a file or API payload that plano later ingests
IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or config path
mitigations: Separate workspaces and config directories
Disable automatic ingestion of agent-generated files
Add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages
Require human review before plano executes instructions from AutoGPT
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGPT has filesystem access and allowlisted egress; plano has broad egress and reads config.yaml. If they share a workspace, file contents touched by AutoGPT can flow into plano’s context or outbound requests. The profiles do not show secrets or PHI, so this is not high, but the shared-file path is credible.
conditions: IF both agents share a directory containing sensitive files
IF plano forwards file-derived context to its upstream API
mitigations: Use separate least-privilege directories
Mount shared folders read-only where possible
Redact sensitive fields before plano ingestion
Restrict outbound destinations for both agents
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGPT can execute shell commands and spawn subprocesses, while plano has broad network egress and reads config files. Even without explicit write permissions on plano, both can mutate shared resources if orchestrated in the same environment. The lack of locking or coordination primitives makes conflicts plausible in default multi-agent setups.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same filesystem tree
IF AutoGPT shell actions modify files that plano also reads or rewrites
mitigations: Assign disjoint resource ownership
Serialize writes through a single orchestrator
Use file locks for shared config paths
Run each agent in separate containers
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGPT can generate outputs that plano may consume through files or API inputs, and plano’s gateway-style role suggests it may route or act on those inputs. Without an explicit verification step, errors from AutoGPT can cascade into plano’s downstream behavior. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF plano treats AutoGPT output as authoritative input
IF no validation layer checks AutoGPT-produced facts before plano acts
mitigations: Insert a verification step between agents
Require schema validation on all handoffs
Log and diff AutoGPT outputs before use
Limit plano to advisory mode for AutoGPT-fed tasks
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking or policy gates

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and show no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch. AutoGPT touches filesystem data and plano handles logs/metrics, but the profiles do not identify regulated data classes or cross-border constraints. With no documented compliance gap, only a small residual risk remains.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into either agent’s workspace
IF deployment policy requires specific residency or retention controls
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared runs
Document retention settings for both agents
Review logging paths before deployment
Keep separate audit trails
requires-engineering: add residency and retention enforcement
